newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates up on German uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates up on German uncertainty.

text.p: Overnight guilder ($11.09) rates surged on Friday to their highest levels since early this year amid uncertainty over German economic trends and its ability to qualify for European monetary union.
Call money changed hands at 3.06 percent on Friday, up from 2.92-95 percent on Thursday. One month-deposits were quoted between 2.90-93 bid. Trade focused on call and short money.
Dealers said recent trends in Germany overshadowed market sentiment.
"Economic developments in Germany don't look good, and there is certainly no reason to hike rates over there," one said.
Another said Germany's poor economic outlook had fuelled EMU uncertainties, which might have triggered the money market rate rise.
Dutch money rates were expected to track their German equivalents upward despite the major gap between central bank and market rates.

"The central bank has manoeuvred itself into a very delicate position. It doesn't want to spoil Duisenberg's track-record by unilaterally hiking rates but technically speaking, the level of the bank's rates does not correspond to the market," one dealer said.
One dealer said this morning's allocation was rather tight, which might have contributed to the rise in overnight money. Others said the market had not expected an ample allocation.
"Savings under the existing contingent are relatively large. The central bank won't lend loads of cheap money forever," one dealer said.
"Rates where higher this morning at opening already, before the allocation was announced," another said.
This morning, the Dutch central bank allocated 2.31 billion guilders to the money market under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent.
Individual banks' applications up to 3.50 billion guilders were met for 8.5 percent, while no subscriptions were awarded above that level.
The pact replaced a facility of 2.80 billion guilders, which expired today. Under the previous pact, the central bank had met applications up to 3.5 million guilders for 11.5 percent.
